Real-time · interactive 3D

The native full-compartment cell

Every filament, motor, clutch, and bead is an explicit particle — rendered full-resolution (no downsampling). The woven actin cortex encloses a microtubule aster from the centrosome, a 3000-bead nucleus, and focal-adhesion clutches gripping the substrate. Structurally stable at native density; a coarse cell (~250 filaments) collapses on its own — the reason everything here is native.

S6 · cell ↔ matrix

The cell remodels a collagen-I matrix

✓ adheres — 10953/10953 clutches on collagen ✓ traction-driven — audit 190× ✓ stable native, V/V₀ = 1.000 △ not yet coherent inward recruitment

The native cell's basal clutches grip a Mikado collagen-I slab; a co-simulation substeps the compliant matrix under the cell's traction. The matrix deforms (gripped-node 266 nm, peak 586 nm) only where the cell pulls — MCF7's real mechanobiology, matching the collagen-I experiment.

Honest caveat. The deformation is present and traction-driven, but the coherent inward pull is only +15.7 nm of the 266 nm — the collagen follows the clutches as the cell settles, rather than being densified inward. Physiological remodeling (inward densification + fiber alignment) needs the two-way coupling + a coherent contractile pull. That is the next session.

The honest record

What was chased, and what was learned

The crawl mechanism was attempted four ways; each was rejected for a specific, correct reason. The conclusion: a real polarized crawl is research-level, and dramatic single-cell crawling is not MCF7 (epithelial, poorly migratory) physiology — so the axis moved to matrix interaction (S6).

  1. Body-force protrusion — front push + uniform reaction. Tore the cell into a 136 µm tube.
  2. Anchor drift — slid the substrate anchors forward. The floor moved, not the cell.
  3. Slip-traction — fixed anchor, forward clutch force. Rigid translation — a sphere sliding, no shape change, MTOC static.
  4. Piece composition — front-poly + rear-depoly + myosin + front-bias adhesion. Perfectly symmetric (skew = 0) — no polarization.
  5. Re-scope — crawl is not MCF7-central. → S6 matrix remodeling, where the validated mechanobiology (cortex, adhesion, traction) does real work.
Two artifacts hardened along the way: the native + full-compartment HARD rule in CLAUDE.md (coarse cells manufacture collapse artifacts), and the recognition that com_drag drift and cortex collapse were both coarse artifacts that vanish at native density.

Next — S6 physiological remodeling

  • Two-way cell ↔ collagen coupling — the cell feels the compliant matrix (biphasic traction vs. stiffness, Chan-Odde).
  • Coherent contractile inward pull → matrix densification + fiber alignment (real remodeling, not clutch-following).
  • Native + full compartments throughout; validate with the displacement-field and stress viewers.
